pairing.description: To complete pairing follow the instructions in “Notifications” under “HomeKit Pairing”.
pairing.title: Pair HomeKit

review.description: {count} entities will be selected for HomeKit.
review.title: Review entity selection

user.description: Choose the domains to be included. All supported entities in the domain will be included except for categorized entities. A separate HomeKit instance in accessory mode will be created for each tv/receiver media player, activity based remote, lock, and camera.
user.title: Select domains to be included

accessory.title: Select the entity for the accessory

bridged_device_triggers.description: Programmable switches are created for each selected device. When a device trigger fires, HomeKit can be configured to run an automation or scene.
bridged_device_triggers.title: Bridged device triggers

data.camera_copy: Cameras that support native H.264 streams

cameras.description: Check all cameras that support native H.264 streams. If the camera does not output a H.264 stream, the system will transcode the video to H.264 for HomeKit. Transcoding requires a performant CPU and is unlikely to work on single-board computers.
cameras.title: Camera configuration

climate.description: Choose which accessory each climate entity uses in HomeKit. Heater Cooler puts the mode, temperature, and the supported fan speed and swing controls on one air conditioner style tile; Thermostat is the classic temperature dial with a separate fan. Automatic keeps the accessory the entity already uses and picks the best fit when it is bridged for the first time. Changing the accessory type keeps the room and name, but HomeKit scenes or automations that used the old controls may need to be recreated.
climate.title: Climate accessory configuration

include.description: Selected domains are included in full, and selected targets are included independently. More specific selections take precedence, and exclusions win conflicts at the same specificity.
include.title: Include and exclude targets

init.description: HomeKit can expose a bridge or a single accessory. Accessory mode supports one entity and is required for TV or receiver media players. In bridge mode, the next screens let you select independent include and exclude targets in addition to entire domains.
init.title: Select mode and domains.

review.description: {count} entities will be selected for HomeKit.
review.title: Review entity selection

yaml.description: This entry is controlled via YAML
yaml.title: Adjust HomeKit options

reload.description: Reloads HomeKit and re-processes the YAML-configuration.
reload.name: [%key:common::action::reload%]

unpair.description: Forcefully removes all pairings from an accessory to allow re-pairing. Use this action if the accessory is no longer responsive and you want to avoid deleting and re-adding the entry. Room locations and accessory preferences will be lost.
unpair.name: Unpair an accessory or bridge
